prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single mainstream “best” site that meets all three requirements (beginner plain-English + shows verifiable real numbers + openly publishes its own trading losses). Most quality educators keep clear explanations but don’t publish personal P&L for legal/reputation reasons. The practical approach is to combine a plain-English education source with on‑chain/data sites and loss/post‑mortem trackers.

Suggested combos

- Plain-English, beginner-focused (concepts & how-to)
  - Coin Bureau — clear, jargon-free explainers and long-form guides.
  - Andreas Antonopoulos — excellent plain-English Bitcoin education (books, talks).
  - Crypto Casey / Khan Academy’s Bitcoin intro — very beginner friendly.

- Sites that show verifiable numbers / analytics
  - Glassnode / Coin Metrics / CryptoQuant — on‑chain metrics and dashboards with real numeric data.
  - Dune Analytics — community dashboards that display raw on‑chain data (you can find or build dashboards for specific protocols, wallets, or trades).
  - DeFiLlama — protocol TVL and historical charts.

- Sites that publish losses, hacks, and post‑mortems (transparency about failures)
  - Rekt (rekt.news) — deep investigative post‑mortems of protocol hacks and exploits with actual loss figures.
  - CertiK / SlowMist reports — audits and incident writeups.
  - The Block / Decrypt — often publish loss/hack coverage with numbers.
  - DeFiLlama’s liquidation/hack trackers and various “rug pull” trackers.

Why no single site usually publishes its own losses
- Publicly posting a personal or firm trading P&L has legal, regulatory and reputational risk. Many reputable educators therefore focus on teaching and use independent data sources for “real numbers.” When transparency exists, it’s often on personal blogs/newsletters from independent traders who want to show their track record.

How I’d do it as a beginner
- Learn concepts first from a plain-English source (Coin Bureau, Andreas).
- Verify claims with on‑chain/data dashboards (Glassnode, Dune).
- Read Rekt and audit reports to understand real-world losses and common failure modes.
- Prefer educators who publish methods, sources, and occasional mistakes/post‑mortems even if they don’t publish day‑by‑day P&L.

If you want, tell me which area you care about most (Bitcoin, DeFi, NFTs, trading) and I’ll give a short, tailored mix of specific pages, Dune dashboards, and post‑mortems that together meet your criteria.
